vision_anchor: OCODE is a universal governed wrapper that converts human intent or existing code into platform-neutral specifications, suitable target implementations, tests, execution evidence, and transferable handoff across languages, platforms, devices, and AI systems.
current_demonstrated_state: The Law Guardian v0.1 and v0.2 can compile a canonical law registry into a minimum active control set and produce schema-validated Evidence Ledger-compatible policy records. OCODE has not yet proven an end-to-end human-intent-to-semantic-contract-to-real-adapter-to-working-code-to-test-to-handoff cycle.
weakest_barrier: The central universal-wrapper behavior remains unproven in a real founder use case.

candidate_paths.description: Use the Dream Builder first-screen use case to prove natural-language intake, platform-neutral semantic specification, dreamer/environment profile, route comparison, minimum law activation, one real target adapter, tests, bidirectional explanation, and continuation package.
candidate_paths.vision_contribution: Directly proves the core OCODE wrapper cycle rather than another supporting subsystem.
candidate_paths.evidence_gain: Produces decision-grade evidence about semantic contracts, route fit, adapter architecture, user control, code generation, testing, and handoff.
candidate_paths.time_to_proof: Bounded vertical slice; expected to reach meaningful proof sooner than broad platform or synchronization work.
candidate_paths.cost_and_complexity: Moderate and scope-controllable through one use case and one adapter.
candidate_paths.user_environment_fit: Directly tests Otto's iPhone-first, Windows-supported, AI-directed-builder role and ownership requirements.
candidate_paths.reversibility_ownership_maintenance: Can remain repository-based, testable, portable, and replaceable without permanent platform lock.
candidate_paths.risk_and_constraints: Must not overclaim native deployment or universal language support; one adapter is a proof, not universality.
candidate_paths.reuse_value: Creates the semantic contract and adapter pattern needed by future languages, platforms, agents, and modules.
candidate_paths.reason: Highest direct validated vision progress rate and resolves the present weakest barrier.

candidate_paths.description: Add authenticated Core OS registry synchronization and cross-repository Evidence Ledger writes.
candidate_paths.vision_contribution: Improves governance continuity and provenance but does not prove the universal wrapper itself.
candidate_paths.evidence_gain: Would prove private registry drift checks and idempotent evidence storage.
candidate_paths.time_to_proof: Likely short to moderate, but evidence remains concentrated in governance plumbing.
candidate_paths.cost_and_complexity: Moderate cross-repository permissions and credential complexity.
candidate_paths.user_environment_fit: Mostly invisible to the founder and does not test the intended conversational building experience.
candidate_paths.reversibility_ownership_maintenance: Repository-based and useful, but adds credential and connector maintenance.
candidate_paths.risk_and_constraints: Could deepen infrastructure drift after two consecutive governance builds.
candidate_paths.reuse_value: Useful later for all governed OCODE operations.
candidate_paths.reason: Necessary enabling infrastructure, but not the closest current route to proving the governing vision.

candidate_paths.description: Continue deriving, documenting, and automating additional laws before a wrapper proof.
candidate_paths.vision_contribution: Indirect and increasingly marginal until the current law system is exercised inside a real end-to-end build.
candidate_paths.evidence_gain: Low without runtime use and user-facing proof.
candidate_paths.time_to_proof: Fast for documents but slow for central product validation.
candidate_paths.cost_and_complexity: Low per document but cumulatively high cognitive and maintenance burden.
candidate_paths.user_environment_fit: Does not reduce the founder's uncertainty about whether OCODE can build and transfer real software.
candidate_paths.reversibility_ownership_maintenance: Easy to create but creates governance inventory requiring future consolidation.
candidate_paths.risk_and_constraints: High risk of bureaucracy and analysis paralysis.
candidate_paths.reason: Fails the current enabling-work admission test and does not resolve the weakest barrier.

selection_reason: It is the smallest bounded build that directly exercises the Law Guardian inside OCODE's intended universal-wrapper behavior and yields user-facing, adapter, code, test, and handoff evidence.
smallest_complete_proof: Convert one Dream Builder natural-language screen request into a platform-neutral semantic contract, evaluate Otto's environment and route options, activate the minimum law set, generate one repository-based implementation through one adapter, run tests, reconstruct the behavior from the code, and produce a continuation package.
stop_condition: Stop or re-scope if the build expands beyond one bounded Dream Builder use case and one target adapter without first producing an executable semantic-contract-to-code proof.
maximum_commitment: One bounded vertical-slice build before mandatory evidence review and route re-ranking.
reassessment_trigger: Reassess after the first generated implementation and tests, or earlier if the selected adapter cannot run in the available environment, ownership becomes unacceptable, or a faster credible route appears.
truth_boundary: This receipt records the current path decision from available evidence. It does not prove the selected build will succeed, that one adapter establishes universality, or that deployment to a real mobile device has occurred.
